studies.label: Pairit ad-creation experiment: Human-AI versus Human-Human teams
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Individuals were randomized on entry and then matched into teams (PDF p. 14). Participant outcomes use heteroskedasticity-robust SEs without stated team clustering; human and AI rating models cluster at the ad level; the additional team-productivity regression uses one row per team with robust SEs.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 15, Section 3.4 (Participants); corroborated by PDF p. 16, Table 1
counts_source.quote: exclude them from all analyses, yielding a final sample of 2,234 participants (1,258 human-AI, 976 human-human).

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: One participant paired with a GPT-4o agent teammate that can chat, write and edit ad copy, select stock images, and generate Dall-E 3 images in the shared workspace. Only the human can submit ads; partner identity is revealed after the task (PDF pp. 11-15).

arms.name: Human-Human
arms.description: Two participants collaborate in the same shared workspace and confirm submissions jointly. Both can also use the Dall-E 3 image-generation interface. The comparison aid is the human teammate (PDF pp. 11, 14-15).

studies.task: Create display ads for a think tank’s year-end annual report by writing headlines, primary text, and descriptions and selecting or generating images during a 40-minute collaboration (PDF pp. 4, 11, 14-15).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI gpt-4o-2024-08-06 agent on Pairit; Dall-E 3 image generation available in both arms
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 3.2, names gpt-4o-2024-08-06; PDF p. 11, Section 3.1, specifies shared Dall-E 3 access. Year refers to the dated GPT-4o model version.

estimates.notes: One analysis row per participant and heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. No team clustering is stated despite the shared workspaces of Human-Human partners. open_items: The paper does not provide a reconciled randomization flow or arm counts at assignment. PDF p. 15 distinguishes entrants, task completers, and the final analyzed sample and reports exclusions only for incomplete Human-Human collaborations; n_randomized is therefore null. The abstract’s random-assignment description uses the final analyzed sample size.

Participant and team totals in Table 1 do not reconcile for Human-Human; the narrative exclusion and attrition figures also do not reconcile (PDF pp. 15-16). Counts are retained exactly as printed; none are repaired or inferred from team totals.

No arm means or arm-level SDs of eligible outcomes are explicitly printed, and no standardized treatment effects are supplied. Regression intercepts, particularly covariate-adjusted intercepts, are not substituted for arm means. The diversity record therefore lacks both arm levels despite retaining the printed raw coefficient and SE.

Arm-specific participant counts for diversity and creator counts for the human- and AI-rated output analyses are not printed. Rating, output, and team observation counts must not be treated as counts of randomized people.

The participant-to-output mapping for jointly confirmed Human-Human ads is not explained. Participant analyses use robust SEs without stated team clustering, and rating analyses cluster by ad rather than creator/team (PDF pp. 15, 19, 21-22, 47, 49, 51-52). Appropriate creator/team-level variance or data would be needed to resolve repeated-output dependence.

The retained human-rater count is unclear: recruitment, entry/completion, prepared ad-sample counts, and reported rating observations are not reconciled (PDF pp. 17, 22). Evaluators are not randomized ad creators.
Ad-copy completion rates have no operational definition or identified coding/scoring method (PDF pp. 48-49); measure remains null.

The paper names productivity, ad quality, and output diversity as primary outcomes (PDF p. 21), but does not identify which outcomes were preregistered as primary; preregistered_primary remains not_stated.

For the excluded field results, the ad-corpus totals and VTR/VTD observation units are not reconciled (PDF pp. 16, 18-20, 25, 53). The displayed field coefficients all control for post-treatment spend; unconditional randomized collaboration effects are not printed.
The paper states that code and data are available upon request (PDF p. 39); the provided records contain no analysis-data supplement. No effects or variances were reconstructed from external data.
